function: Above the physical layer: LSTM traffic and rain-attenuation forecasts feed gateway load balancing and beam-to-gateway matching, solved by non-learned optimization and genetic algorithm (p. 1-2, 11).
notes: Exclude, above_phy. Page 1 holds the title Data-Driven Beam-to-Gateway Matching and Adaptive Load Balancing for Multi-Beam GEO Satellite Systems, matching the DOI. It is a research article with simulation results (p. 13-15), so codes 1, 2 and 7 do not apply. The only learned element is a stacked multi-horizon LSTM that forecasts per-beam traffic demand and per-gateway rain attenuation (p. 2: "These forecasts are then used as inputs to an adaptive genetic algorithm that performs proactive, capacity-aware B2G matching and load balancing"); it takes no beam, power or resource decision. Capacity allocation and beam-to-gateway matching come from a convex problem and from AGA, GA, ACO and WLB heuristics, none learned (p. 8-11), for load balancing under QoE and blocking-probability targets: traffic steering and network management above the physical layer, with traffic prediction as the learned task. A reviewer who reads the matching as a non-learned physical-layer function could use no_learning instead.
